_note_scope: ONE per-frame record - this is the unit the dataset is built from. Contains ONLY what varies frame to frame. Static rig/calibration lives in ego_config.json; run config lives in scene_description.json; CARLA settings, conventions, encodings and the class map live in CARLA_config.json.
_loader_contract: Underscore-prefixed keys are documentation. The loader MUST strip them RECURSIVELY before use - notes appear inside iterable containers (see sensor_files) and an unstripped loader will treat a prose sentence as a file path.
_note_frame_id: Composite key, padded per CARLA_config.naming_convention: {scene_id:03d}_{carla_frame:06d}. carla_frame is the integer from world.tick() - the authoritative cross-sensor sync key in synchronous mode, reproducible given the same seeds. (scene_id, carla_frame) is the real primary key; frame_id is the derived string. Zero-padding makes lexicographic sort == numeric sort.
_note_timestamp: CARLA simulation time in seconds since episode start. NOT wall clock - wall clock is not reproducible.

sensor_files._note: Paths relative to the scene's s3_prefix. Explicit, never inferred. NOTE: the depth and instance_seg PNGs are ENCODED buffers, not literal images - see sensor_encoding in CARLA_config.json for the decode formulas. Reading them naively yields garbage.

ego_pose._note: Ego pose in the CARLA world frame. Sensor world pose = this composed with T_sensor_to_ego from ego_config.json.
ego_pose._note_units: position in meters, rotation in DEGREES (roll/pitch/yaw), linear velocity in m/s, angular velocity in deg/s.

actors._note_id: 'id' is the raw CARLA actor.id and is ONLY unique within an episode - actor 123445 in scene 1 and scene 2 are different vehicles. 'global_actor_id' ({scene_id:03d}_{actor_id}) is the dataset-wide unique key. Join on global_actor_id everywhere; this becomes load-bearing the moment tracking exists (Phase 0 supporting task).
actors._note_class: 'class' here is the RAW base_type straight from the blueprint - it is NOT the final dataset class. The KITTI writer applies CARLA_config.class_map to produce the training label. Recording blueprint_id + base_type means class re-maps and collapses are free offline; you never re-run the sim to change your mind about the class list.
actors._note_velocity: Recorded at capture even though the detection hero does not need it. Capture is one-shot and GPU-expensive; this field is nearly free now and requires a full re-run to add later. Needed for tracking and lead-vehicle relative speed.

bounding_box_world._note: Resolved to WORLD frame at capture time: actor.bounding_box (actor-local) composed with actor.get_transform(). Storing world-frame directly means the offline pipeline never redoes this composition.

actors._note_source: Signs are NOT CARLA actors. The visible mesh box comes from world.get_environment_objects(CityObjectLabel.TrafficSigns); the posted speed comes from map.get_all_landmarks_of_type('274'). Associate by proximity. Two consequences: (1) blueprint_id/base_type are null, (2) signs have no instance-seg ID, so their visibility check uses the DEPTH camera, not instance segmentation.
actors._note_class: Raw record keeps class='speed_sign' + listed_speed_kph as an attribute. The KITTI writer flattens these into a per-value class (speed_sign_90) via CARLA_config.class_map, because KITTI allows exactly one class string per label line.

_note_actors: Capture-time records are UNFILTERED - every actor CARLA reports, including ones occluded or out of frustum. Visibility filtering happens offline (step 8.iii/8.iv). Do not filter on the GPU instance: keeping raw means the filter is re-tunable for free.
_note_no_visibility_field: Deliberately absent. 'visible' is a DERIVED property computed offline against the instance-seg (vehicles) or depth (signs) buffers. Baking it into raw capture would freeze one filter threshold into data that costs GPU hours to regenerate.
